speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate a skin lesion with potential oncologic implications; can you describe exactly what the spot looks like, including its size, shape, color, and how it has changed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC).

The presence of a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the penis in a 62-year-old male with a significant smoking history and prior failed treatments for syphilis is highly suspicious for penile SCC. The similar lesion on his finger raises concern for a secondary site or concurrent lesion. I need to confirm the extent of the disease before proceeding.

REQUEST TEST: Penile_biopsy.
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray (to screen for metastasis).
